lines.operation: commandArgs(FALSE) reads the startup arguments. grep matches the start of a string using ^, and value=TRUE retains the matched strings. The result is a character vector of length zero or one locating the file run by Rscript.

lines.code: source_files <- vapply(sys.frames(), function(frame) if (is.null(frame$ofile)) "" else frame$ofile, character(1))
lines.operation: sys.frames() reads the call frames. vapply applies a function to each frame, requiring one character string per result. When source() runs a script, ofile records its path; frames without a path return an empty string.

lines.code: script_path <- if (any(nzchar(source_files))) tail(source_files[nzchar(source_files)], 1) else if (length(script_argument)) sub("^--file=", "", script_argument[1]) else file.path("en", "R", "ch06.R")
lines.operation: if selects the source path: use the last non-empty ofile when called through source(); otherwise remove the --file= prefix. Code pasted into the R console at the project root defaults to this lesson’s script path. The output is one path string; [] indexing starts at 1.
length checks that the path has one element. 1L is integer 1, and !is.na excludes missing values. stopifnot requires every condition to be TRUE and stops otherwise.

dirname extracts the script directory. file.path joins the path two levels up to the project root; normalizePath requires that directory to exist. The result is independent of the current working directory.
source reads and executes the shared R definitions for reading the CSV, mathematical functions and manual model fitting. Only base R is used; no TMLE package is required.
Read the original CSV, calculate empirical probabilities for the eight (x,a,y) cells and return the resulting data and model in a list. Later calculations use these same patient records.
In this exercise, keep empirical g fixed and let b specify coefficients of candidate additional components. Perform the weighted linear-algebra projection manually and return a list.

lines.code: cat("candidate norm squared =", demo$candidate_second_moment, "; projection =", demo$projection_second_moment, "; residual =", demo$residual_second_moment, "\n")
lines.operation: Display three weighted squared norms to check the Pythagorean decomposition. Each scalar has units of squared probability differences.
Subtract the two eight-element vectors, take absolute values with abs, then use max to reduce them to one maximum error.
Display the maximum numerical difference between the projection and the canonical gradient in this model with fixed g.
